unitTitle: B1 · Tell the story clearly: before, during and after
title: Grammar: Plus-que-parfait: show what had happened before
subtitle: B1 · Unit 1: B1 · Tell the story clearly: before, during and after

steps.title: Plus-que-parfait: show what had happened before
steps.body: A2 already gives you passé composé for completed events and imparfait for background or habit. Add plus-que-parfait when one past event was already complete before another past moment. Form it with the imparfait of avoir or être plus the past participle. Keep the order clear: background (il pleuvait), earlier event (le cours avait commencé), then the event you are telling (je suis arrivé). With être, agree the participle with the subject. Do not use plus-que-parfait for every past action.

steps.title: Plus-que-parfait: show what had happened before
rows: La réunion avait commencé quand je suis arrivé.
The meeting had started when I arrived.
Il pleuvait pendant que nous attendions.
It was raining while we waited.

steps.prompt: The class was already underway when I arrived. Which sentence marks the earlier event?
options: Le cours a commencer quand je suis arrivé.
Le cours avait commencé quand je suis arrivé.
steps.explain: Avait commencé marks an event completed before the arrival.

steps.prompt: Which form best sets an ongoing background?
options: Il pleuvait pendant que nous attendions.
steps.explain: The imparfait describes the ongoing background.

options: An event completed before another past reference point
steps.explain: It places one past event earlier than another past moment.
